entries.spiritual_meaning: The Divine Itself — Infinite Divine Love as the absolute origin of all being
entries.definition: As a father is the origin of offspring, and 'greatness' signifies what is immeasurable, the Father of Greatness corresponds to the Infinite Divine Love from which all things proceed — the Lord's own esse, self-subsistent and beyond all finite comprehension.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Conflates Love and Wisdom; text consistently reserves Wisdom for the Mother/Spirit.

variant_readings.reading: the Lord in His infinite being
variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Accurate but less specific; 'Divine Love' captures the correspondential function better.

entries.notes: Swedenborg: 'The Divine Love is the esse of all life' (DLW 1). In this text the Father is always hidden, never directly manifest — corresponding to the Lord's infinite esse that can only be known through its proceeding forms. The Father's 'five limbs' (mind, thought, insight, counsel, consideration) correspond to the five essential faculties of the Divine itself.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Celestial Human — the Lord as the Divine Rational descending into spiritual combat
entries.definition: As the 'first' human is the archetype of all humanity, and as a 'man' signifies the rational good that combats evil, the First Man corresponds to the Lord's own celestial-rational principle that descends into the deepest temptation to confront and overcome evil at its root.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Used in a few passages but 'Celestial Human' is more consistent with the combat function.
Captures the volitional aspect but the term 'Human' requires the full rational-human meaning.

entries.notes: The First Man's five sons = five faculties of celestial perception. His descent and ascent map to what Swedenborg describes as the Lord's temptation-combats (AC 1690). The five garments (fire, wind, water, light, air) are the five external truths by which the Divine engages evil. The First Man 'standing between the borders' before casting himself down corresponds to the Lord at the boundary between the Divine and the created.

natural_variants: the Living Spirit the Father of Life
entries.spiritual_meaning: Divine Truth Proceeding from the Lord in its operative, judicial, and governing power
entries.definition: As 'spirit' signifies the operative agency of truth, and 'living' denotes what flows from the Divine, the Living Spirit corresponds to the Lord's Truth as it proceeds with power to order, judge, construct, and sustain all things — the active mode of the Divine in creation and redemption.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Used once; Providence is more consistently assigned to the Third Ambassador.
Good but less specific than 'Divine Truth Proceeding' which captures the Swedenborgian procedere.

entries.notes: The Living Spirit's seven works (§325–§333) map to a complete cycle of regeneration. Its five sons correspond to five faculties of governing truth distributed through discrete degrees. The Living Spirit always constructs and orders — corresponding to the Lord's Truth as it creates spiritual form. Cf. Swedenborg: 'The Lord through the Divine Truth proceeding from Him created the universe' (TCR 76).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Mediating Divine Principle — Divine Truth proceeding as universal manifestation and purification
entries.definition: As an 'ambassador' mediates between a sovereign and the world, the Third Ambassador corresponds to the Divine Truth that proceeds into manifestation between the inmost heaven and the external mind, displaying the divine image to purify wisdom from its admixture with falsity.

variant_readings.reading: Divine Providence proceeding into all things
variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Used in some passages but 'mediating' better captures the ambassador function.
Accurate for certain contexts but too narrow for the full range of the term.

entries.notes: The Ambassador's key act is displaying his 'image' — corresponding to the Lord making the Divine Human visible to the understanding. When the rulers react to this image, it produces the separation of good from evil that drives the whole narrative. The Ambassador's ten works (§340–§350) describe a complete regenerative sequence. This figure mediates between what Swedenborg calls the celestial and natural degrees.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Divine Truth proceeding from Love that generates all spiritual life — the formative matrix of Divine Wisdom
entries.definition: As a 'mother' gives birth and nourishes, and 'Life' signifies what flows from the Divine, the Mother of Life corresponds to the Divine Truth that proceeds from Divine Love to generate and sustain all spiritual life — the Lord's Wisdom as it flows forth to create and nurture.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Too generic; the Mother-function specifically involves generation of life.
Captures one aspect but misses the generative/maternal function.

entries.notes: The Mother of Life is consistently the first emanation from the Father — corresponding to Wisdom proceeding from Love. She 'spent a long time in the Father' (§234–§237) before being summoned — the infinite state in which Divine Wisdom dwells in Divine Love before proceeding. She corresponds to what Swedenborg calls the Divine Existere as distinct from the Divine Esse.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Divine Wisdom in its radiant, saving, and illuminating manifestation
entries.definition: As 'splendour' is the visible radiance of an interior light, Jesus the Splendour corresponds to Divine Wisdom as it becomes radiant and manifest — the Lord's Truth made visible in glory, liberating the mind from falsity through illumination.

variant_readings.reading: Divine Truth in its fullness and glory
variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Accurate but less specific than 'Wisdom in its radiant manifestation.'
Good synonym but 'radiant' captures the 'splendour' correspondence better.

entries.notes: Jesus the Splendour's advent is likened to one who uproots bad trees and plants good ones (§160–§161) — corresponding to the Lord's work of destroying false perceptions and implanting true ones. His twelve wisdoms (§27) = twelve truths derived from good. His ten vehicles (§84–§90) describe the ten degrees through which the Divine descends into the human mind.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Pure uncorrupted Wisdom — the affection of truth in its pristine, innocent form
entries.definition: As a 'virgin' signifies what is uncorrupted and undefiled, and 'light' signifies truth, the Virgin of Light corresponds to the pure affection of truth proceeding from good — Divine Wisdom in its innocent, uncorrupted state that captivates even the powers of evil by her beauty.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Narrower; 'uncorrupted Wisdom' covers the full range of the term's function.

entries.notes: The Virgin displays herself to attract the powers of evil, who release captive light in their longing — corresponding to how the beauty of genuine truth draws out what is good even from states dominated by evil. She serves as 'guide' in the elevation of purified elements (§847). Her distinction from what is 'continent' (§789–§795) maps to the difference between pristine wisdom that never fell and restored wisdom that was purified after contamination.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Divine Enlightenment of the Understanding — interior illumination that awakens and gathers
entries.definition: As 'mind' signifies the interior intellectual faculty and 'light' signifies truth, the Light Mind corresponds to the Divine influx that illuminates the understanding from within — the awakening power that rouses the dormant spirit and gathers scattered truths into unity.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Good synonym; chosen rendering captures the awakening function more fully.

variant_readings.reading: Divine Wisdom operating within the understanding
variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Accurate but generic.

entries.notes: The Light Mind is 'the awakener of those who sleep, the gatherer of the scattered' (§121). When it enters the body (§565–§569), it humbles the guards at the orifices and opens them to good — corresponding to the moment of regeneration when Divine truth overcomes the proprium's resistance. It forms the 'new man' (§843).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Sustaining Column of Divine Truth — the axis connecting lowest to highest through which purified good ascends
entries.definition: As a 'pillar' upholds a structure and 'glory' signifies divine truth made manifest, the Pillar of Glory corresponds to the sustaining axis of Divine Truth through which all purified good ascends from the natural degree to the celestial — the Lord's Truth as it connects and supports all discrete degrees.

variant_readings.reading: the upright axis of Divine Good made manifest
variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Reverses the Good/Truth attribution; the Pillar is consistently a Truth-function.

entries.notes: The Pillar is consistently described as bearing all things up and as the pathway of ascent. The First Man's head is 'placed on the body of the Pillar' (§320), indicating that the celestial ruling love operates through this sustaining truth-structure. Cf. Swedenborg on the Word as the connecting medium between heaven and earth.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The proprium — the self-derived will in its utter opposition to the Divine, the origin of all spiritual death
entries.definition: As 'matter' in Manichaean cosmology is the formless, lifeless substrate from which evil creates, it corresponds to the proprium — the human selfhood as it exists apart from God, which fashions all false appearances of life from what is spiritually dead.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Accurate but less concise than 'the proprium' alone.
Captures the active aspect but misses the formative/shaping function.

entries.notes: Matter is always 'the thought of death' and 'the sculptress' — the proprium that shapes dead forms into the appearance of life. She 'gave strength for the war' (§32) — the proprium empowers evil's assault against good. Swedenborg: 'The proprium of man is nothing but evil' (AC 210).

entries.natural_term: King of the realms of Darkness
entries.spiritual_meaning: The ruling self-love — the sovereign principle of all evil, the love of dominion from the proprium
entries.definition: As a 'king' rules and 'darkness' signifies falsity from evil, this entity corresponds to self-love as the governing principle that organizes all evils and falsities into a counterfeit kingdom opposed to the Divine order.

variant_readings.reading: the sovereign of the realms of falsity from evil
variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Accurate but wordy; 'ruling self-love' is more precise correspondentially.

entries.notes: His five shapes (lion, demon, eagle, dragon, fish) = five genera of evil organized under self-love. His five properties (darkness, putridity, ugliness, bitterness, burning) = five essential qualities of evil. He 'knows not what is far from him' (§54–§55) — self-love perceives only what is immediately present to sensation, never what is interior or remote.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The fully realized form of the regenerated human — the completed Grand Man
entries.definition: As a 'statue' is a completed formed image, the Last Statue corresponds to the ultimate perfected form of the regenerated human — the final gathering of all purified good and truth into one complete spiritual body, corresponding to the Grand Man of heaven.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Suitable for some contexts but 'completed Grand Man' captures the collective dimension.

entries.notes: The Last Statue 'gathers all life and sculpts itself' (§163) — the completed human form is not imposed from without but self-organizing from within, as each regenerated good finds its proper place. Its ascent marks the final separation of good from evil. Cf. Swedenborg's Maximus Homo.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Wisdom — divine truth as perceived and received by the understanding
entries.opposite_sense: Falsity from evil (when 'light' is stolen, scattered, or mixed with darkness)
entries.definition: As natural light illuminates and makes visible, spiritual light corresponds to wisdom or divine truth, which illuminates the understanding and makes spiritual realities perceptible.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Often used interchangeably with 'wisdom' but 'wisdom' is more consistent across the corpus as the primary rendering.
Used for 'day' contexts; 'wisdom' is the broader and more primary correspondence.

entries.notes: Swedenborg: 'The light of heaven is the Divine Truth' (HH 126). In this text, light is always what is scattered, mixed, purified, and gathered — precisely the pattern of wisdom as it descends into the natural mind and must be separated from falsity.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Falsity from evil — the absence and privation of divine truth
entries.definition: As natural darkness is the absence of light, spiritual darkness corresponds to falsity from evil — the state in which divine truth is absent and the understanding is occupied by what is false, flowing from self-love.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Used for 'death' specifically; darkness = falsity is the consistent correspondence.

entries.notes: Darkness as one of the five dark elements specifically corresponds to the total privation of good and truth — the deepest form of spiritual darkness. As a general term it always = falsity from evil.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Divine love — celestial love as the inmost animating principle
entries.opposite_sense: Self-love — consuming desire that devours (when 'dark fire', 'fire of the body', or infernal fire)
entries.definition: As natural fire gives warmth and consumes, spiritual fire corresponds to love — divine love when holy and living, self-love when dark and destructive. Fire is the inmost element because love is the inmost principle of life.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Specific to the positive sense; 'divine love' is broader and primary.

entries.notes: Fire is always the inmost of the five elements in both light and dark series. Living fire = divine love; dark fire = self-love. The fire of the body (§8) = self-love blazing in the natural mind. The 'great fire' at the end = the final consuming love of judgment. Swedenborg: 'In the Word, fire signifies love in both senses' (AC 934).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Truth — living truth that purifies and regenerates
entries.opposite_sense: Falsity — corrupted, falsified truth (when dark water, poison, or sea of falsities)
entries.definition: As natural water cleanses and sustains life, spiritual water corresponds to truth that purifies and nourishes the understanding. Dark or poisonous water corresponds to falsified truth.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Accurate but narrower; 'truth' alone covers the full range.

entries.notes: The 'ship of living waters' = vessel of living truth (the moon's ship). Water as one of the five light elements = truth in its living form. Dark water = falsified truth, the corruption most deeply embedded in the channels of the understanding.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Spiritual influx — the living breath of the spirit that flows into the understanding
entries.opposite_sense: False persuasion — vain reasoning, the force of falsity (when dark wind or storm-wind)
entries.definition: As wind is invisible moving air that carries force, spiritual wind corresponds to the influx of the spirit — the animating flow of truth into the understanding. Dark wind corresponds to the persuasive force of falsity.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Used when wind = garment/doctrine; 'spiritual influx' is the broader primary meaning.

entries.notes: Wind as garment (§315–§316, §395) specifically = the doctrine of understanding/rational truth as an external covering. Dark wind = the world of vain reasoning; its king is eagle-faced = predatory rationality.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The sphere of spiritual perception — the rational atmosphere of the mind through which all influx passes
entries.definition: As air is the universal medium through which all life breathes, the living air corresponds to the sphere of spiritual perception — the rational medium that sustains and pervades all understanding. It is the outermost of the five light elements, remaining unwounded in combat.

variant_readings.reading: the living influx from the Divine
variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Too generic; 'sphere of spiritual perception' captures the specific air-correspondence.

entries.notes: The living air is unique: it alone was not wounded in the first combat (§511–§512), corresponding to the innermost rational sphere that falsity cannot penetrate. It gave its garment to its four brothers — the rational sphere sustains all other faculties. Swedenborg associates the atmosphere of heaven with the sphere of spiritual perception.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Obscurity of understanding — confused falsity arising from self-love
entries.definition: As smoke obscures vision and arises from combustion, spiritual smoke corresponds to the confused falsity that rises from the fire of self-love — the darkening of the understanding that prevents clear perception of truth.
entries.notes: The world of Smoke is the first/chief of the five dark worlds. Its king came up from the depth — the obscurity of understanding is the primary evil from which all spiritual assault originates. Its ruler is 'the head of all wickedness' (§49). Its taste is salty = craving for conjunction of evil with falsity.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Celestial good (positive) / semblance of celestial good (negative, in the kingdom of Darkness)
entries.opposite_sense: The counterfeit appearance of good that masks sovereign evil
entries.definition: As gold is the most precious and enduring of metals, it corresponds to celestial good. When attributed to the King of Darkness, it signifies that sovereign evil clothes itself in the semblance of good to deceive.
entries.notes: Gold is explicitly the body of the King of the realm of Smoke — the most interior falsity disguises itself as the highest good. Swedenborg: gold = celestial good (AC 113).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Spiritual truth (positive) / falsified truth (negative, in the realm of Water)
entries.opposite_sense: Falsified truth — truth distorted to serve evil ends
entries.definition: As silver is the second precious metal, it corresponds to spiritual truth. When attributed to the dark realm of Water, it signifies truth that has been falsified — made to appear genuine while serving evil.
entries.notes: Silver = body of the rulers of Water. Swedenborg: silver = spiritual truth (AC 1551). In the dark sense, the 'sweet taste' of Water's silver = the seductive delight of falsified truth.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Natural good (positive) / perverted natural good (negative, in the realm of Fire)
entries.opposite_sense: Natural good corrupted by self-love
entries.definition: As copper is a base but useful metal associated with warmth, it corresponds to natural good. In the dark realm of Fire (self-love), it signifies natural good perverted by selfish desire.
entries.notes: Copper = body of the rulers of the world of Fire. Its taste is sour = aversion to genuine good. Swedenborg: copper = natural good (AC 425).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Natural truth (positive) / hardened natural falsity (negative, in the realm of Wind)
entries.opposite_sense: Falsity hardened into impenetrable resistance against truth
entries.definition: As iron is hard and cutting, it corresponds to natural truth in its lowest form. In the dark realm of Wind (vain reasoning), it signifies falsity hardened into unyielding resistance against genuine truth.
entries.notes: Iron = body of rulers of the world of Wind. Its taste is 'sharp' = the cutting, divisive quality of falsity. The King of Darkness is 'harder than every iron' (§52). Swedenborg: iron = natural truth in its lowest form (AC 425).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The densest, basest falsity — falsity without any residual truth
entries.definition: As lead is the densest and basest of common metals, it corresponds to the densest falsity — falsity entirely devoid of truth. Tin adds the element of counterfeit truth.
entries.notes: Lead/tin = body of the rulers of pure Darkness. Its taste is bitterness = interior torment. Swedenborg: lead = dense falsity (AC 8298).

entries.spiritual_meaning: A state of spiritual life — a heavenly society or discrete degree of the Divine order
entries.opposite_sense: When 'aeons of Darkness': states or realms of evil organized by self-love
entries.definition: As an 'aeon' signifies an age or realm, it corresponds to a discrete state of spiritual life — a society in heaven or a degree of the mind's interior organization. The aeons of light are the infinite heavenly societies proceeding from the Lord.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Used in some passages but 'state of spiritual life' is more versatile across the corpus.

entries.notes: The 'new aeon' (§287, §371, §460) = the regenerated spiritual state. 'Aeons of greatness' = the infinite states within the Divine itself. The text consistently uses 'aeon' for what Swedenborg calls 'societies of heaven' or 'degrees of the mind.'

entries.spiritual_meaning: A containing form or vessel of doctrine — the organized receptacle through which divine influx is received and conveyed
entries.definition: As a ship contains and conveys passengers across water, a spiritual ship corresponds to a doctrinal form — the organized system of truths that contains and conveys good across the expanse of natural knowledge.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Specific to the sun's ship; 'vessel of doctrine' is the general correspondence.

entries.notes: Ship of the day (living fire) = doctrine of celestial love/illumination. Ship of the night (living waters) = doctrine of truth operating in states of obscurity. Ships are always 'containing forms' — they receive, carry, and transmit. Swedenborg: 'Ships signify doctrines' (AR 406).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The natural mind — the plane of consciousness where spiritual life takes external form
entries.opposite_sense: When 'earth of Darkness' or 'land of death': the natural mind wholly given over to falsity and evil
entries.definition: As the earth is the ground upon which life grows and rests, it corresponds to the natural mind — the external plane of consciousness that receives seeds of truth and good, or that is dominated by falsity and evil.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: 'Natural mind' is more specific and functionally accurate.
Only applies to 'new earth of light'; primary rendering covers both senses.

entries.notes: 'Three earths' (§6, §34) = three degrees of the natural mind. 'Light earth' = the natural mind receptive to good. 'Earth of darkness' = natural mind dominated by evil. The 'new earth' (§382) = regenerated external mind. Swedenborg: 'Earth = the church, or the external of man' (AC 566).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Discrete degrees of the understanding — the structural framework of truth that separates interior from exterior
entries.definition: As a firmament separates waters above from waters below, a spiritual firmament corresponds to a degree of the understanding that distinguishes and separates interior truths from exterior ones — the structural truth-framework of the mind.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Accurate but 'degrees of the understanding' is more functionally precise.

entries.notes: Ten firmaments = the ten discrete degrees of heavenly order. Seven firmaments above the wheel = seven degrees of the rational understanding. Swedenborg: 'The firmament is the internal man which separates the externals from the internals' (AC 24).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The providential cycle of spiritual reformation — the revolving order of knowledges through which good and evil are processed
entries.definition: As a wheel turns in cycles, the cosmic wheel corresponds to the cycle of Divine Providence — the revolving system of spiritual knowledges through which regeneration proceeds, evil is restrained, and good is elevated.

variant_readings.reading: the revolving cycle of natural knowledges
variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Specific to the zodiacal wheel; the broader 'providential cycle' covers all usages.

entries.notes: The wheel has 'twelve seals' = twelve constraining truths in their fullness. It functions as a 'great mirror' for divine discernment (§361). The wheel has no root in the earth (§479–§481) — the system of providential knowledge is not grounded in the merely natural. Evil powers are 'suspended' on the revolving wheel so that 'they comprehend not the place wherein they are set' (§467).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Elevated state of love or celestial perception — a state of the will raised above the natural plane
entries.opposite_sense: When 'mountains of Darkness': states of self-exaltation in falsity from evil
entries.definition: As mountains rise above the surrounding plain, spiritual mountains correspond to elevated states of love — exalted conditions of the will where celestial good is received. Dark mountains = self-exaltation.
entries.notes: 'Four mountains' (§6, §464) = four elevated states of good that surround and protect the natural mind. Mountains of Darkness (§56) = states of self-exaltation. Swedenborg: 'Mountains = the celestial things of love' (AC 795).

entries.spiritual_meaning: A containing doctrinal form — a structure that receives and holds good or evil
entries.opposite_sense: When 'dark vessel' or 'vessel of death': containing form emptied of life, holding evil
entries.definition: As a vessel contains liquid, a spiritual vessel corresponds to a containing doctrinal form — an organized structure capable of receiving and holding either good and truth, or evil and falsity.
entries.notes: 'Three vessels' (§6, §391, §464) = three containing forms that surround the mind (of water/falsity, darkness/blindness, fire/self-love). These are expelled from interior to natural mind to the hells (§424–§435). The process of their expulsion = the Swedenborgian doctrine that evils must first be brought into consciousness before they can be removed.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Restraint upon evil — the divine ordering that confines falsity and prevents it from spreading
entries.opposite_sense: When evil binds good: bondage, spiritual captivity
entries.definition: As bonds physically restrain, spiritual bonds correspond to the restraining power of divine order that confines evil within limits. The 'lump' is the ultimate consolidated mass of evil permanently sealed.
entries.notes: The 'eternal chain' (§155, §390) = the permanent restraint of evil after final judgment. The 'lump' (§14, §17, §260, §264) = the final consolidated mass of unredeemable evil. Swedenborg: 'The hells are kept in order by the Lord' (HH 543).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The intermediate sphere of spiritual life — the boundary between interior heavenly states and exterior natural states
entries.definition: As a 'zone' is a boundary region, the spiritual zone corresponds to the intermediate sphere where good and evil meet — the world of spirits between heaven and hell, or the limbus between the spiritual and natural degrees of the mind.
entries.notes: The Ambassador is 'king of the zone' (§304) — mediating divine truth governs the intermediate sphere. The zone is where the fifteen paths of spiritual progression are drawn (§753). Corresponds to Swedenborg's 'world of spirits.'

entries.spiritual_meaning: A governing principle of spiritual authority — a seat of divine or infernal dominion
entries.definition: As a throne is the seat from which a sovereign rules, a spiritual throne corresponds to a governing principle — a locus of authority from which spiritual governance proceeds.
entries.notes: Eighteen thrones: nine in the interior heavens, nine in the intermediate sphere. Swedenborg: 'Throne = the Divine in heaven and the church' (AR 14).

entries.spiritual_meaning: A constraining truth that confirms and fixes — a confirmation or determination that cannot be altered
entries.definition: As a seal authenticates and fixes, a spiritual seal corresponds to a constraining truth that confirms spiritual order — a determination that fixes things in their proper state so they cannot be moved from divine order.
entries.notes: 'Twelve seals' in the wheel (§357) = twelve constraining truths of faith in their fullness. 'Sealed with the seal of truth' (§569) = confirmed in divine order. The seal of the zodiac upon the sea giant (§438) = the imprint of all spiritual knowledge upon the composite selfhood.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A pathway or channel of spiritual influx connecting interior to exterior degrees
entries.definition: As a conduit carries fluid between locations, a spiritual conduit corresponds to a channel of influx — the living connection between a celestial power and its corresponding natural vessel through which good ascends and evil descends.
entries.notes: Three conduits connect heaven to earth (§470): (1) celestial powers to their corporeal forms, (2) doctrinal forms to perceptions (trees), (3) governing rational loves to proprial will (flesh). Conduits are spiritual and cannot be cut by the revolving wheel (§494–§497) — influx is of spiritual substance and self-restoring.

entries.spiritual_meaning: External truth clothing interior good — truth in its accommodated, outward-facing form
entries.opposite_sense: When 'rags' or 'tattered': devastated or degraded truths
entries.definition: As garments clothe and protect the body, spiritual garments correspond to external truths that clothe and protect interior good — truth accommodated to reception at a given degree.
entries.notes: Five garments of the First Man = five external truths clothing celestial good for combat. Three garments of the Living Spirit (wind, fire, water) = three doctrines (understanding, love, truth) used to purify the mind. 'Light garment' (§82) = garment of truths woven from wisdom. 'Rags' (§719) = wisdom devoured and scattered. Swedenborg: 'Garments = truths' (AC 1073).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Means of spiritual reception and communication between degrees of the mind
entries.definition: As gates control passage in and out, spiritual gates correspond to the faculties of reception by which good and truth enter or leave the mind — the openings between discrete degrees.
entries.notes: Gates 'open before and shut behind' the divine influx (§353) — each degree receives the proceeding and transmits it forward. The orifices of the body (§562–§566) = the openings of the external person through which good or evil enters. 'Four gates per world' (§840) = four modes of reception at each degree.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The ruling love — the governing principle from which all subordinate faculties depend
entries.definition: As the head governs the body and is the seat of consciousness, the spiritual head corresponds to the ruling love — the inmost governing principle upon which all subordinate affections and faculties depend.
entries.notes: The King of Darkness's 'lion-faced head' = governing love of dominion from self-love (§50). 'Should his head be cut off, the entire body will die' (§319) = if the ruling love is destroyed, all spiritual life perishes. 'All the small heads hang from the great head' (§520) = all particular evils depend from the one ruling self-love.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The will — the seat of love, the inmost center that governs all other faculties
entries.definition: As the heart circulates life-blood to the whole body, the spiritual heart corresponds to the will — the center of love that receives, guards, and distributes all that the other faculties bring to it.
entries.notes: 'The heart is like the king. All the advisers are placed with him' (§556). The heart receives deposits from all five senses and guards them (§555) = the will receives from all faculties and governs. 'The heart accords to the wheel of the rotating sphere' (§679) = the will is the living center of the whole cycle of life.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Intellectual sight — the faculty of understanding by which spiritual realities are perceived
entries.definition: As the eye sees and makes things visible, spiritual sight corresponds to the understanding — the faculty by which spiritual truths and states are perceived and distinguished.
entries.notes: Two eyes = two aspects of intellectual sight. 'Two light ships' = two eyes of the spiritual cosmos (§591). The eye's storehouses (§550) = the memory of the understanding. 'While it perceives by day, yet come the night it shall not perceive' (§837) = the understanding perceives in states of illumination but not in states of darkness.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Obedient reception — the faculty of hearing and receiving truth from the Word
entries.definition: As ears receive sound, spiritual hearing corresponds to the reception of truth — the obedient faculty by which divine truth is received into the understanding.
entries.notes: Ears' storehouses preserve 'every sound for a thousand days' (§551) = the memory of doctrinal truth persists through complete states. 'Good enters through the ears and the eyes' (§569) = good is received through obedience and understanding.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The faculty of discrimination and communication — the power to distinguish truth from falsity and to express doctrine
entries.definition: As the tongue tastes and speaks, the spiritual tongue corresponds to the dual faculty of discriminating the quality of truth (taste) and communicating it outwardly (speech).
entries.notes: The tongue 'proclaims, reprimands, and reveals about everything inside and outside' (§593). It is one of the five members that form the word (§823). The faculty of the tongue is the first of the five 'dens' of the dragon (§801) = the first refuge of the ruling falsity is in outward communication.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Divine Love and Wisdom as the ruling source of spiritual illumination
entries.definition: As the natural sun is the source of light and heat for the world, the spiritual sun corresponds to the Lord's Divine Love and Wisdom — the source of all spiritual illumination, warmth of charity, and life.

variant_readings.reading: divine love as the ruling good
variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Captures the love-aspect but the sun in this text is primarily the source of illumination/wisdom.

entries.notes: The sun accomplishes seven works (§625–§632): illumination, peace, awakening, nourishing, driving evil into hiding, healing, and manifesting heavenly glory. Five archetypes in the sun (§641–§646): light, beauty, peace, liberation, and strength. Three further archetypes (§648–§651): perpetual fullness, surpassing wisdom, supreme height. The sun and moon are 'strangers' to the evil powers (§677) — they are from the Divine, not from the dark realm.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Faith — divine truth in its reflected, natural, and fluctuating form
entries.definition: As the moon reflects the sun's light and waxes and wanes, the spiritual moon corresponds to faith — truth received in a derivative, reflected form that fluctuates according to the state of the receiver.
entries.notes: The moon's ship = vessel of living truth. The moon wanes unlike the sun (§649) — faith fluctuates while divine love is constant. Swedenborg: 'The moon = faith from charity' (AC 30).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Knowledges of good and truth — particular insights of spiritual understanding
entries.definition: As stars are individual points of light, spiritual stars correspond to particular knowledges of good and truth — the discrete insights that illuminate the understanding.
entries.notes: Swedenborg: 'Stars = knowledges of good and truth' (AC 2495). The stars are bound on the revolving wheel (§461–§469) — knowledges are organized within the cycle of providence.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Perception — the organized faculty of knowing and producing works (good or evil)
entries.opposite_sense: When 'bad tree': perception rooted in self-intelligence; when 'Cross of Light': divine truth suffering in natural forms
entries.definition: As a tree grows from a root, produces branches and fruit, a spiritual tree corresponds to a perception — the organized faculty of knowing that grows from its root (origin in good or evil) and produces works (fruit).

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Specific to the 'good tree'; primary rendering covers both senses.

entries.notes: 'Good tree' = perception rooted in wisdom; 'bad tree' = perception rooted in self-intelligence. 'Five trees' (§48) = five kinds of perverted perception from five genera of evil. 'Cross of Light' (§723) = divine good scattered and bound within natural perceptions. Swedenborg: 'Trees = perceptions' (AC 103).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Works — the spiritual effects produced from perception and love
entries.definition: As fruit is the product of a tree, spiritual fruit corresponds to works — the spiritual effects and deeds that proceed from a person's perception and ruling love.
entries.notes: Good fruit = works of charity. Bad fruit = evil deeds. 'Bad fruit did not arise from the good tree' (§17) = works of evil cannot proceed from genuine wisdom. Swedenborg: 'Fruits = works of life' (AC 3146).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The general body of natural knowledge — the vast expanse of sensory and factual knowing
entries.definition: As the sea is a vast body of water, the spiritual sea corresponds to the general body of natural knowledge — the accumulated mass of sensory, factual, and natural truths upon which doctrinal systems navigate.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Contextual variant; primary meaning is the neutral body of natural knowledge.

entries.notes: The 'salty inner sea' (§427) = natural knowledge corrupted by the residue of evil. The sea is where doctrinal 'ships sail' (§432). The 'sea giant' (§438–§446) = the composite selfhood formed from accumulated sensory knowledge. Swedenborg: 'Sea = the collection of knowledges' (AC 28).

entries.spiritual_meaning: A stream of truth or doctrine flowing through the mind
entries.definition: As a river flows from a source across the land, a spiritual river corresponds to a stream of truth or doctrine that flows through the understanding.
entries.notes: 'The Tigris is but one river among thousands' (§601) = natural knowledge is a tiny portion of the vast body of divine truth. Seven rivers flowed to each ruler (§598) = a fullness of truth was poured into each state of evil.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Obscured truth — truth in a state of mixture or accommodation, not yet fully clear
entries.definition: As a cloud obscures sunlight, a spiritual cloud corresponds to truth in an obscured state — truth that is mixed with natural elements and not yet fully transparent to the understanding.
entries.notes: Clouds ascend toward the Virgin of Light (§765–§774) — obscured truths rise toward pure wisdom for purification. Different types of cloud (fire, water, wind, light) = different types of obscured truth being purified. Swedenborg: 'Clouds = the Word in the letter' (AC 4060).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Influx of truth from heaven — the gentle descent of divine truth into the natural mind
entries.definition: As rain descends from clouds to water the earth, spiritual rain corresponds to the influx of divine truth descending from the spiritual into the natural mind, nourishing its growth.
entries.notes: Dew = gentle communications of good. Mist = truth in obscurity. Swedenborg: 'Rain = influx of truth' (AC 2702).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The lust for dominion from self-love — the predatory desire to rule
entries.opposite_sense: In positive context: the power of celestial good (rare in this text)
entries.definition: As a lion is the most powerful predator that dominates other animals, the lion corresponds to the love of dominion — the desire to rule from self-love, the foremost of evil affections.
entries.notes: Lion-faced is always the head (ruling love) of the King of Darkness and the ruler of the world of Fire. Swedenborg: 'Lion = the power of falsity from evil, or celestial good in its power' (AE 278).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Predatory rationality — the intellectual faculty perverted to seize and dominate
entries.definition: As an eagle soars high and swoops to seize prey, the eagle corresponds to rationality perverted to predatory ends — the intellectual power that elevates itself and then seizes upon what is below.
entries.notes: Eagle-faced = the shoulders/wings of the King of Darkness = the power of elevation perverted. Belongs to the world of Wind = false persuasion/vain reasoning.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The falsification of truth — the systematic perversion of genuine truth into falsity
entries.definition: As a dragon is a serpentine monster that devours, the dragon corresponds to the systematic falsification of truth — the interior appetite that takes genuine truth and perverts it into falsity from within.
entries.notes: Dragon-faced = the belly of the King of Darkness = interior appetite. The dragon is also the 'thought of the body' with fourteen heads (§797–§803) = the complete system of self-derived intelligence. Swedenborg: 'The dragon = those who falsify truths' (AR 537).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Base corporeal knowing — the lowest form of natural knowledge perverted to infernal ends
entries.definition: As fish live in the depths of water, the fish corresponds to the lowest and most external form of natural knowing — corporeal knowledge that, when perverted, serves only base and infernal purposes.
entries.notes: Fish-faced = the tail of the King of Darkness = ultimate sensory expression. Belongs to the world of Water = perverted truth. 'Caught them like fish in the sea' (§180) = captured natural knowledges from the waters of the external mind.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Precious interior truth of faith — a truth of supreme value formed through suffering
entries.definition: As a pearl is formed within a shell through irritation and is the most precious of gems from the sea, it corresponds to a precious truth of faith formed through temptation — drawn up from the depths of natural knowledge.
entries.notes: The First Man is brought up from the abyss 'the way a pearl is brought up from the sea' (§326). Swedenborg: 'Pearls = knowledges of good and truth' (AR 727).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Foundational truth — truth that is firm, confirmed, and immovable
entries.definition: As a rock is the firmest and most enduring of natural substances, spiritual rock corresponds to foundational truth — truth that is absolutely confirmed and cannot be moved.
entries.notes: Three great rocks (§602–§606): (1) the Pillar of Glory = sustaining divine truth, (2) the new luminous earth = regenerated natural mind, (3) the great thought from Jesus = divine perception. The 'Adamant of Light' = indestructible truth from divine good. Swedenborg: 'Rock = the Lord as to Divine Truth' (AC 8581).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The perception of spiritual good — the interior delight of celestial affection sensed by the spirit
entries.opposite_sense: When 'stench' or 'putridity': the spiritual corruption of evil perceived with revulsion
entries.definition: As perfume is perceived by the sense of smell and produces delight, spiritual perfume corresponds to the perception of celestial good — the delight that arises when the spirit perceives what is genuinely from the Divine.
entries.notes: 'The perfume of the Father' (§205) = the sphere of divine good perceived interiorly. 'Sweet perfume that takes away all affliction' (§373) = the perception of celestial good removes spiritual suffering. Swedenborg: 'Odor = perception' (AC 925).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Doctrine — the encompassing truth by which things are drawn and held
entries.opposite_sense: When evil's net: the persuasion by which evil ensnares good
entries.definition: As a net encompasses and draws in, a spiritual net corresponds to doctrine — the systematic arrangement of truths by which dispersed goods and affections are drawn together and held.
entries.notes: The First Man's net is 'the living soul' (§40); the Ambassador's net is 'his light image' (§41); Jesus's net is 'his wisdom' (§42). Evil's net is 'fire and lust' (§44). Swedenborg: 'Net = doctrinal things' (AC 9141).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Spiritual temptation and combat — the interior conflict between good and evil
entries.definition: As war is the conflict between opposing forces, spiritual war corresponds to temptation — the interior combat between the forces of good (from the Divine) and evil (from the hells) within the human spirit.
entries.notes: Five wars (§179–§185) = five stages of regeneration through combat. The First Man's war is always the Lord's temptation-combats. Swedenborg: 'Wars in the Word signify spiritual combats' (AC 1664).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The separation of good from evil and truth from falsity within the mind
entries.definition: As purification removes impurities from a substance, spiritual purification corresponds to the progressive separation of good from evil and truth from falsity within the regenerating mind.
entries.notes: Purification is the central process of the entire text. The Ambassador 'purified the light by his image' (§7). The three vessels are purified and expelled (§391–§435). Purification always involves bringing impurities into consciousness before removal — matching Swedenborg's doctrine exactly.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Elevation to interior and celestial states — the progressive interiorization of the spirit
entries.definition: As ascending means moving upward, spiritual ascent corresponds to elevation from exterior to interior states — from the natural toward the spiritual and celestial degrees of the mind.
entries.notes: The sequence of ascent (§715): light → fire → water → wind → air → answer → summons → Mind → Pillar → First Man → Ambassador → aeons = the progressive interiorization through all discrete degrees.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Proceeding into lower/exterior/natural states — divine accommodation or spiritual fall
entries.definition: As descending means moving downward, spiritual descent corresponds either to the Divine proceeding into lower degrees (accommodation) or to the fall of the spirit into more external and natural states.
entries.notes: Divine descent is always for the purpose of redemption. Evil's descent is its fall into more external states. The ten vehicles of Jesus (§84–§90) = ten degrees of the Lord's descent.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Collecting scattered goods and truths into unity — the reconstitution of the spiritual self
entries.definition: As gathering collects what is scattered, spiritual gathering corresponds to the reunification of scattered goods and truths — the progressive restoration of the regenerating mind to wholeness and order.
entries.notes: The Light Mind is 'the gatherer of the scattered' (§121). The Last Statue 'gathers all life' (§163). The counsel of life 'will gather itself in and sculpt itself' (§43).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Giving determinate spiritual form — establishing an organized and permanent state
entries.opposite_sense: When evil sculpts: giving form to falsity, creating false appearances of life
entries.definition: As sculpting gives form to shapeless material, spiritual sculpting corresponds to the act of giving determinate form to spiritual substance — establishing organized states of good or evil.
entries.notes: Matter is 'the sculptress' who fashions dead forms (§31). The Last Statue 'sculpts itself' (§163). The Father 'sculpted' the emanations (§233–§237). Evil also sculpts — the sea's 'thought' shaped the sea giant (§441). Positive sculpting = divine formation; negative = the proprium's counterfeiting.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The utter subjugation and rendering powerless of evil — or the binding of good within natural forms
entries.opposite_sense: When light is 'crucified in darkness': good/truth bound and profaned within the realm of falsity
entries.definition: As crucifixion fixes and renders immobile, spiritual crucifixion corresponds to the total subjugation and rendering powerless — either of evil (by divine truth) or of good (by evil forces that bind it within natural forms).
entries.notes: 'He crucified it' (§4) = the Divine Human subjugated evil utterly. 'The light was crucified in the darkness' (§167) = wisdom was subjected to profanation in the realm of falsity. The Living Spirit 'crucified' the rulers (§32–§33, §35) = divine truth fixed the ruling evils in their place within the created order.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The active pursuit and reclamation of captive good and truth from the dominion of evil
entries.opposite_sense: When evil hunts: the ensnaring of good by self-love and concupiscence
entries.definition: As hunting pursues and captures, spiritual hunting corresponds to the active pursuit and reclamation of scattered and captive goods and truths — the Divine operation that seeks and draws forth what evil holds captive.
entries.notes: Four divine hunters (§39–§43): First Man, Third Ambassador, Jesus, and the counsel of life. Four infernal hunters (§44–§47): King of Darkness, evil counsel, lust, spirit of Darkness. Each divine hunter has a specific net, ship, and sea.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Successive changes of state — the soul passing through form after form without rest
entries.definition: As transmigration is the passage of a soul from body to body, spiritual transmigration corresponds to the endless cycling through successive states of falsity — the condition of the unregenerate mind that passes from one false appearance into another without finding rest.
entries.notes: Always negative: the guidance of the bad tree leads to 'transmigration from type after type' (§14). The tenth work of the Ambassador brings about 'transmigrations in the zone' (§350). Even restored wisdom that was not fully purified 'goes up and comes down in transmigration' (§794).

entries.spiritual_meaning: A state of spiritual illumination — a complete period of divine operation
entries.definition: As day is the period of light, spiritual day corresponds to a state of illumination — a complete period in which divine truth operates and makes things visible.
entries.notes: Four great days (§23–§28) = four states of divine illumination descending through successive degrees. Three great days (§366–§376): (1) the Lord's descent/combat, (2) reign in the regenerated state, (3) final unveiling of the Divine. Swedenborg: 'Day = a state of light' (AC 488).

entries.spiritual_meaning: A state of spiritual obscurity — a period dominated by falsity from evil
entries.definition: As night is the period of darkness, spiritual night corresponds to a state of obscurity — a period in which falsity from evil dominates and truth is hidden.
entries.notes: Four great nights (§29–§38) mirror the four days: (1) the realm of pure falsity, (2) Matter as fashioner, (3) the five corporeal realms, (4) the law of Sin. Night does seven evils (§633–§640): darkness, fear, revolt, sleep, ugliness, evil emerging, and displaying the sign of primordial evil.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Interior rest — the heavenly state when goods and truths are conjoined and all conflict ceases
entries.definition: As peace is the absence of conflict and the presence of harmony, spiritual peace corresponds to the interior rest that comes when the will and understanding are conjoined in good and truth, and the warfare of temptation ceases.
entries.notes: Peace is one of the five mysteries of the First Man (§91–§93). The peace of descent = the peace of ascent (§100) — divine conjunction is unbroken through temptation. 'Bound with a chain of peace' (§569) = confirmed in charity. Swedenborg: 'Peace corresponds to every good of heaven' (HH 284).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The stilling of the proprium's activity — the state of interior receptivity when self-activity ceases and Divine influx is received
entries.definition: As silence is the absence of self-generated sound, spiritual silence corresponds to the stilling of the natural mind's own activity — the state in which the proprium ceases its noise and the spirit becomes receptive to divine influx.
entries.notes: The Father exists 'in calm and hiddenness' (§139) — the Divine Itself dwells in infinite peace. The counsel of life 'was established in silence' (§163). The Mother was 'established in his inner storehouses in quiet and silence' (§237). 'The silence at the time when his heart is opened to the love of God' (§833) — the stilling of the proprium is the precondition for receiving divine love.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The conjunction of love — the union of interior affections between the Divine and the human
entries.definition: As a kiss unites two persons in affection, a spiritual kiss corresponds to the conjunction of love — the moment when the Divine and the human will unite in mutual affection.
entries.notes: One of the five mysteries of the First Man. 'The kiss of affection and love' (§95). The Light Form 'calms the person with the kiss and her quiet' (§106). Swedenborg: 'Kisses = conjunction from affection' (AC 3574).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The communication of divine power — the bestowal of spiritual strength
entries.definition: As the right hand is the hand of power and action, a spiritual right hand corresponds to the communication of divine power — the bestowal of spiritual strength from a higher to a lower degree.
entries.notes: One of the five mysteries. The Mother gave the First Man the right hand (§94) = Divine Wisdom communicated power for combat. Swedenborg: 'The right hand = omnipotence' (AC 878).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The transmission of interior authority — the communication of spiritual governance from higher to lower
entries.definition: As the laying on of hands transfers authority, spiritual laying on of hands corresponds to the transmission of governing power — the communication of interior authority from a supreme good to what is subordinate.
entries.notes: The first laying on of hands: the Mother armed the First Man (§97). The second: the Living Spirit established the First Man as 'leader of his brethren in the new aeon' (§104).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The divine calling — the Lord's influx of truth that awakens and calls the human spirit toward regeneration
entries.definition: As a summons calls someone to come, the spiritual summons corresponds to the Lord's calling — the influx of divine truth that penetrates into the natural mind and calls the spirit to awaken and ascend.
entries.notes: Always paired with 'obedience.' Together they constitute the 'counsel of life.' The summons descends headfirst (§805) — divine truth enters the lowest states first. 'A peace letter and greeting' (§742) = influx of divine peace.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The will's reception and responsive acknowledgment — the human spirit's answer to the divine call
entries.definition: As obedience is the response to a command, the spiritual obedience corresponds to the will's receptive acknowledgment — the human spirit's free response to the divine calling, ascending from below as the summons descends from above.
entries.notes: The obedience ascends while the summons descends — the will's response rises to meet the truth that descended. Together they are 'the father and the mother' (§146) = active influx and receptive will. 'The answer wished to ascend with the summons' (§830).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The intellectual or understanding aspect — what pertains to truth and rational thought
entries.definition: As 'male' signifies the active, rational, and intellectual principle, spiritual 'male' corresponds to the understanding — what pertains to truth, rational discernment, and intellectual perception.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Specific to the dark context; primary rendering covers both positive and negative senses.

entries.notes: Male and female together = the complete mind (understanding + will). In the dark realm, 'five male and five female' = five of false understanding and five of corrupted will. Swedenborg: 'Male = the intellectual' (AC 54).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The volitional or will aspect — what pertains to love, affection, and desire
entries.definition: As 'female' signifies the receptive, affective, and volitional principle, spiritual 'female' corresponds to the will — what pertains to love, desire, and affection.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Specific to dark context only.

entries.notes: In the final separation (§389), 'male divided from female' = intellectual evil divided from volitional evil. Swedenborg: 'Female = the voluntary' (AC 54).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Delight of good — the pleasantness of genuine truth received in love
entries.opposite_sense: When 'sweet taste' of Water (§61): seductive delight of falsified truth
entries.definition: As sweetness pleases the palate, spiritual sweetness corresponds to the delight of genuine good — or, in its perverted form, the seductive delight of falsified truth that pleases the natural mind.
entries.notes: The Father's sweetness (§207) = blessedness flowing from Divine Love. The sweet taste of Water (§61) = the seductive sweetness of falsified truth. Swedenborg: 'Sweetness = delight of good and truth' (AC 5620).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Interior torment — the grief of unmixed evil, the anguish of the unregenerate state
entries.definition: As bitterness is repugnant to the taste, spiritual bitterness corresponds to interior torment — the essential grief and anguish that constitutes the life of evil when stripped of all good.
entries.notes: The King of Darkness's bitterness is 'his own soul' (§51) = the essential life of evil IS torment. Bitterness of the world of Darkness (§62). Salty inner sea = corrupted knowledge tasting of bitterness (§427). Swedenborg: 'Bitterness = what is unpleasant and grievous from evil' (AC 7854).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The craving for conjunction of evil with falsity — the corrosive quality of perverted desire
entries.definition: As salt preserves but also corrodes, spiritual saltiness corresponds to the craving for the conjunction of evil with falsity — the corrosive appetite that perverts what is received.
entries.notes: Salty = taste of Smoke's world (§58) = the mode by which obscure falsity appropriates its evil works. The salty inner sea (§427) = natural knowledge corrupted by the residue of expelled evil.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Aversion — the rejection of genuine good
entries.definition: As sourness is the taste that puckers and repels, spiritual sourness corresponds to aversion — the active rejection and repulsion of genuine good.
entries.notes: Sour = taste of the world of Fire (§59) = the mode by which self-love rejects genuine good.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Concupiscence — the disordered desire of self-love that enslaves the will
entries.definition: As lust is desire driven by selfish appetite, spiritual lust corresponds to concupiscence — the disordered desire that flows from self-love and seeks to possess, consume, and dominate.
entries.notes: Always paired with 'fire' (self-love) as its companion. 'Fire and lust' together = self-love and concupiscence, the originating evil and its derivative. Swedenborg: 'Concupiscence = the affection of evil' (AC 8910).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The lust to appropriate what belongs to divine good — the hatred of all life and good that belongs to another
entries.definition: As envy is the resentful desire for what belongs to another, spiritual envy corresponds to the primal orientation of evil — the lusting desire to possess and dominate what belongs to the Divine.
entries.notes: 'The entirety of envy is this first nature' (§727) — envy is the primordial proprium. 'Death's essential quality is envy' (§223) — the origin of spiritual death is the lust to appropriate what is not one's own.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Divine Love — the essential life flowing from the Lord that conjoins and vivifies all things
entries.definition: Love, in its genuine sense, is the Divine Esse itself — the essential life from the Lord that flows into all things and conjoins them in mutual regard.
entries.notes: 'Love is the Father of Greatness' (§608) — love IS the Divine. 'These two are a single living body, the Father and his love' (§608) — the Divine Esse and Divine Love are one. Swedenborg: 'The Divine Love is the life itself of all things' (DLW 1).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Primal spiritual death — the fundamental orientation of evil that destroys all good
entries.definition: As hate is the opposite of love, spiritual hatred corresponds to the fundamental orientation of evil — the primal spiritual death that welled up from the proprium and destroys all that is of the Divine.
entries.notes: 'Hate is the first death that welled up' (§609). Hatred = the abomination, self-love from self-love, infernal from infernal, evil from evil (§610). Swedenborg: 'The opposite of love is hatred' (HH 400).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Most Ancient Church — the first and highest spiritual state of humanity; or the natural will and understanding formed in the divine image
entries.definition: As Adam is the first human, he corresponds to the Most Ancient Church — the earliest celestial humanity that received wisdom directly from the Divine. Adam and Eve together = the natural will and understanding fashioned by self-derived powers after the divine image.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Applies when Adam is fashioned by rulers; the broader 'Most Ancient Church' applies to §570–§579 and §611.

entries.notes: Three things distinguishing Adam (§611–§614): (1) the divine image, (2) proper arrangement through divine faculties, (3) the seal of the entire spiritual universe. Adam as fashioned by the rulers = the natural self created in an imitation of the Divine form. Swedenborg: 'By Adam is meant the Most Ancient Church' (AC 478).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The volitional faculty of the Most Ancient Church — the receptive will; or the natural will as appropriated by self-love
entries.definition: As Eve was formed from Adam, she corresponds to the will-aspect of the most ancient church — the receptive faculty of affection. When fashioned by the rulers, she represents the natural will as appropriated by self-love.
entries.notes: 'Eve bore forth from a rib of Adam's flesh' (§730) = a faculty was derived from the innermost natural proprium. Swedenborg: 'Eve = the proprium vivified by the Lord' (AC 151).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The proprium in its corporeal form — the selfhood as it manifests in the lowest natural degree
entries.definition: As flesh is the outermost corporeal substance, spiritual flesh corresponds to the proprium in its corporeal manifestation — the selfhood as experienced in the lowest natural and sensory degree of the mind.

variant_readings.reading: the five forms of the proprium
variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Narrower; 'proprium in corporeal form' covers the full range.

entries.notes: 'Five fleshes' = five orders of proprial will. The flesh 'walks in the world' (§13) = the proprium operates in external life. 'Worlds of flesh' (§34–§35) = the fully externalized states of selfhood. Swedenborg: 'Flesh = the proprium' (AC 148).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Divine Good made manifest through wisdom — the conjunction of love and truth in the Lord
entries.definition: As 'beloved' signifies what is cherished by affection and 'lights' signify wisdoms, the Beloved of the Lights corresponds to the Divine Good that is cherished within all illumination — the Lord as the union of love and truth.
entries.notes: The Beloved is 'the one who is honoured' (§66) — divine good glorified through wisdom. 'All glory and honour' begins from the Beloved (§114). Cf. Swedenborg: the Lord as the Bridegroom of the Church.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Divine Ordering Wisdom — the power that constructs the new interior state of the regenerating mind
entries.definition: As a builder constructs structures according to a plan, the Great Builder corresponds to the Divine Wisdom that organizes and constructs all interior structures of the mind — the architect of spiritual form.
entries.notes: The Builder 'built the new aeon for a newness, for a resting place for the fathers of light; also for a place of binding and a prison for the enemy' (§302) — the new spiritual state serves as both heaven for the regenerate and hell for evil. The simile of the skilled carpenter (§526) describes divine providence shaping unformed natural good.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Divine Good governing through truth in the interior rational — the sovereignty of celestial glory
entries.definition: As a king governs with honor, the King of Honour corresponds to the Divine Good that governs through truth in the seventh (innermost rational) degree — the sovereign presence of celestial glory that presides over all lower degrees.
entries.notes: Dwells in the seventh firmament (§288, §311) = the innermost rational degree. The wheel of stars turns before him (§356–§361) = the cycle of knowledges is ordered under his gaze. His will is 'placed in the wheel' (§356) = divine purpose pervades the whole ordering.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Completeness of faith and truth — all things of spiritual order in their fullness
entries.opposite_sense: When 'twelve shadows' or 'twelve spirits of error': the complete structure of falsity
entries.definition: As twelve is the number of completion in spiritual order, it corresponds to all things of faith and truth in their fullness — the complete circle of spiritual reality.
entries.notes: Twelve hours of day = twelve qualities of illumination. Twelve hours of night = twelve qualities of obscurity. Twelve judges = twelve principles of discernment. Twelve signs of zodiac = twelve governing states of spiritual progression. Swedenborg: 'Twelve = all things of faith' (AC 577).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The full complement of spiritual faculties — completeness in a given degree
entries.definition: As five is the number of completeness within a single degree (five senses, five fingers), it corresponds to the full complement of spiritual faculties at a given level — the complete set of capacities through which the mind operates.
entries.notes: Five light elements, five dark elements, five sons of First Man, five sons of Living Spirit, five limbs of the good/bad tree, five garments, five fleshes, five storehouses, five watches — the fivefold structure pervades the entire text. Each set of five = the complete set of faculties at that degree.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Completeness in discrete degrees — the full triad of celestial, spiritual, and natural
entries.definition: As three signifies what is complete through its degrees, it corresponds to the completeness of discrete levels — typically the celestial, spiritual, and natural degrees through which the Divine flows into created life.
entries.notes: Three earths = three degrees of the natural mind. Three vessels = three containing forms. Three garments = three doctrines. Three seasons = three epochs of redemption. Three rocks = three foundational truths. Swedenborg: 'Three = what is complete' (AC 2788).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Malformed and incomplete spiritual productions — quasi-goods and distorted affections born from evil exposed to truth
entries.definition: As an abortion is a failed birth, spiritual abortions correspond to malformed and incomplete spiritual productions — distorted affections and perverted goods that are generated when evil is exposed to the form of divine truth but cannot sustain genuine spiritual life.
entries.notes: Abortions 'fell to the ground' (§349, §171) — malformed spiritual productions descend to the natural plane. They are generated when the rulers are exposed to the Ambassador's image — when evil encounters divine truth it produces monstrous counterfeits.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A monstrous composite of falsity — the aggregate selfhood formed from the residue of all natural knowledge perverted by self-love
entries.definition: As a giant is a monstrous oversized being, the spiritual giant corresponds to the monstrous composite selfhood formed from the accumulated residue of natural knowledge shaped by concupiscence — a counterfeit form of life vastly exceeding natural proportions.
entries.notes: The sea giant is formed from the residue of the wheel's purification (§438–§441) — the composite selfhood is constituted from the sediment of spiritual processes. The beast from the sea (§449, §541) = a monstrous evil that arises from the aggregate of falsities. The Adamant of Light subdues it (§449).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Pristine — wisdom that was never contaminated by falsity
entries.definition: As 'virginal' signifies what is uncorrupted and undefiled, spiritual virginity corresponds to wisdom that never descended into mixture with falsity — truth that remained in its original celestial purity.
entries.notes: Virginal vs. continent (§788–§796): pristine wisdom that never fell vs. restored wisdom that was purified after contamination. The Light Mind entering the elect = 'virginal' (§795). Swedenborg: 'Virgins = affections of genuine truth' (AE 863).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Restored — wisdom that was mixed with falsity, purified, and returned to holiness
entries.definition: As 'continent' signifies self-restraint after indulgence, spiritual continence corresponds to wisdom that descended into mixture with falsity, was purified through temptation, and returned to a holy state.
entries.notes: The 'new man purified from the old man' is 'continent' (§795). A person who 'has a woman in the world and afterwards cleanses himself' (§796) = understanding that was conjoined with worldly affection and then renounced it.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Indestructible Divine Truth — truth from divine good that cannot be broken
entries.definition: As adamant is the hardest substance that nothing can cut, the Adamant of Light corresponds to indestructible truth proceeding from divine good — the ultimate truth that cannot be broken, shattered, or overcome by any falsity.
entries.notes: The Adamant humbles the beast between mountains (§449) = indestructible truth subdues monstrous evil within elevated states of good. The Adamant governs the third watch (§684) = the unyielding truth of the Lord governs the degree from the rational down to the natural.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The foundational sustaining power — the divine principle that upholds all from the lowest natural degree
entries.definition: As a porter carries burdens and stands at the threshold, the Porter corresponds to the foundational divine power that sustains all things from the lowest natural level — the guardian principle at the boundary between the natural and the infernal.
entries.notes: The Porter stands upon the great earth with 'four fastenings under his feet' (§679, §686) = the sustaining power rests upon the outermost natural with four restraints upon infernal forces below. Three earths are above the Porter's head (§449, §679) = three natural degrees rest upon this foundation.

summary.consistency_assessment: The spiritual readings converge very well across the corpus for the major entities: Father of Greatness = Divine Love, First Man = Celestial Human, Living Spirit = Divine Truth Proceeding, light = wisdom, darkness = falsity from evil, fire = love/self-love, earth = natural mind. These are rock-solid throughout. Moderate divergence occurs with the Third Ambassador (rendered as 'Providence,' 'mediating principle,' or 'Divine Rational' depending on chapter context — all describe the same function from different angles). The greatest systematic divergence concerns the five light elements: some chapters render them as the five faculties of perception, others as five constituent goods/truths. This is not random but reflects the text's own fivefold architecture — the same five function differently at different degrees. The taste-correspondences (salty, sour, sharp, sweet, bitter) are remarkably stable across the single chapter in which they appear. The body-cosmos correspondence (§679, §702–§711) is internally consistent and maps precisely to Swedenborg's Grand Man doctrine. The per-chapter readings diverge most on secondary entities (Beloved of the Lights, King of Honour, Great Builder) which appear less frequently and whose function is more contextual.
summary.five_fold_systems: The text contains multiple interlocking fivefold systems that map onto each other: (1) Five Light Elements: fire, wind, water, light, air = love, influx, truth, wisdom, perception — the five faculties of the spiritual mind. (2) Five Dark Elements: smoke, fire, wind, water, darkness = obscurity, self-love, false persuasion, falsity, total privation — the five genera of evil. (3) Five Sons of the First Man = five faculties of celestial good, corresponding to the five garments he wears into combat. (4) Five Sons of the Living Spirit = five faculties of governing truth, sustaining the created order. (5) Five Limbs of the Good/Bad Tree: consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind = reception, guidance, seeing, understanding, willing — mapped to five ascending degrees from outer communion to the Divine Itself (good tree) or five descending degrees from death's law to the ultimate mass of evil (bad tree). (6) Five Metals: gold, copper, iron, silver, lead = celestial good, natural good, natural truth, spiritual truth, dense falsity — the five corporeal forms of the five dark worlds. (7) Five Tastes: salty, sour, sharp, sweet, bitter = five modes of evil's appropriation. (8) Five Storehouses = five origins of evil. (9) Five Fleshes = five orders of the proprium. (10) Five Shapes of the King of Darkness: lion, demon, eagle, dragon, fish = dominion, pure evil, predatory rationality, falsification, base knowing. All these fivefold systems are parallel: each describes the same five-degree structure from a different angle (substance, quality, faculty, taste, form, animal). The key interlocking is: Element → World → King → Metal → Taste → Shape, all mapping to one spiritual reality.
summary.key_findings: 1. FIRE IS ALWAYS INMOST: In both light and dark series, fire occupies the position of the inmost element — divine love or self-love. This confirms that love is the esse of all life in both heaven and hell. 2. THE AIR REMAINED UNWOUNDED: Of the five light elements, only the living air (sphere of rational perception) was not penetrated by evil (§511–§512). This means the rational faculty, when truly from the Divine, is invulnerable — a doctrine matching Swedenborg's teaching that the Lord's rational was never conquered. 3. THE THREE VESSELS DOCTRINE exactly parallels Swedenborg's teaching on vastation: evils cannot be removed directly from the interior to hell; they must first be brought into conscious awareness in the natural mind (§424–§435). 4. THE SUMMONS-OBEDIENCE PAIR operates as the fundamental mechanism of all spiritual conjunction — the descending call and the ascending response are the 'father and mother' (§146) of regeneration, making this pair the most structurally important in the entire text. 5. THE INVERSION PRINCIPLE (§804–§808): when understanding looks into natural truth, everything appears inverted — what is highest in wisdom appears lowest. This corresponds to the law that spiritual realities appear inverted in the natural degree. 6. THE SEVEN WORKS OF THE SUN (§625–§632) map precisely to seven stages of regeneration: illumination, peace, awakening, nourishing, hiding evil, healing, and manifesting glory. 7. THE BODY-COSMOS CORRESPONDENCE (§678–§712) is the most detailed mapping in the text and corresponds exactly to Swedenborg's Maximus Homo doctrine. 8. THE VIRGINAL/CONTINENT DISTINCTION (§788–§796) reveals a teaching about two kinds of regenerated wisdom: pristine wisdom that was never contaminated, and restored wisdom that was purified after falling — a distinction not found this clearly in Swedenborg but fully consistent with his doctrine. 9. THE TWELVE JUDGES (§283–§296) present a complete system of divine discernment operating through all twelve degrees of spiritual order — from the Divine Itself down to the counsel of Providence. 10. THE TEXT'S OWN ARCHITECTURE REVEALS CORRESPONDENCES the per-chapter readings missed: specifically, that 'sculptor/Matter' is always the proprium as FASHIONER rather than mere substance, and that 'the zone' is consistently the Swedenborgian 'world of spirits' — the intermediate state between heaven and hell.
